page.title: Tenant Advocate Review
page.intro: The request requires that any increase be able to withstand review by tenant-friendly San Francisco advocates and lawyers. This page documents the free and low-cost review channels that officially exist, and turns the legal requirements into a review checklist a tenant attorney would apply. It does not claim that a government source can certify an increase in advance. {{S19}} {{S21}} {{S25}} {{F-11}}

sections.heading: 1. Why independent scrutiny is realistic in San Francisco
sections.body: Tenants can obtain free Rent Board counseling, free or low-cost legal help, free legal clinics, and a Tenant Right to Counsel program for eviction proceedings; they can also challenge an increase at no charge with no filing deadline. An unlawful increase can be null and void and can lead to a rent refund. {{S21}} {{S22}} {{S25}} {{S19}} {{S12}}

table.caption: Official tenant review and assistance channels

rows.item: Rent Board counseling
rows.value: Free; 415-252-4600; weekdays 9 am–12 pm and 1–4 pm
rows.basis: "Cost: Free … We provide counseling on subjects related to the Rent Ordinance. We cannot give legal advice."

rows.item: Unlawful rent increase petition (Form 516C)
rows.value: No charge; no time limit
rows.basis: "There is no charge for filing the petition. There is no time limit for filing a petition."

rows.item: Pending increase not yet effective (Form 518)
rows.value: Tenant Summary Petition
rows.basis: "This petition is for tenants who have received a rent increase notice that is clearly unlawful on its face and has not yet gone into effect."

rows.item: Hearing
rows.value: Arbitration before a Rent Board Administrative Law Judge; no attorney required
rows.basis: "The hearing process is designed so that no one needs an attorney, although parties are entitled to have an attorney or other authorized representative assist them at the hearing."

rows.item: Free legal clinics (Rent Board Referral Listing)
rows.value: Three free legal clinics every month for low-income Bay Area residents
rows.basis: "The clinics offer free, limited legal advice and referrals."

rows.item: Tenant advocacy organisations listed by the Rent Board
rows.value: Housing Rights Committee of SF, San Francisco Tenants Union, Tenants Together, Bay Area Legal Aid, Asian Law Caucus and others
rows.basis: Organisations listed under "Tenant Resources" in the official Rent Board Referral Listing.

rows.item: Tenant Right to Counsel
rows.value: Free legal assistance for residents facing eviction and free full-scope legal assistance for eligible cases
rows.basis: "In June 2018, San Francisco voters passed the No Eviction Without Representation Act to establish the Tenant Right to Counsel program …"

rows.item: Free legal help for eviction court papers
rows.value: Eviction Defense Collaborative, 415-659-9184
rows.basis: "If you are a tenant who has received eviction court papers, you can call 415-659-9184 … for free legal help."

rows.item: Consequence of a defective increase
rows.value: Null and void; possible rent refund
rows.basis: "Any rent increase which does not conform with the provisions of this section shall be null and void." "… your tenant may be entitled to a rent refund."

rows.item: Official certification that an increase passes tenant-lawyer review
rows.basis: A legal opinion, not an officially verifiable value. Left blank by rule.

sections.heading: 2. The review checklist
sections.body: Each row is a control derived from an official source. A reviewer would expect documentary evidence for every one of them. Rows that cannot be confirmed on this project are left blank and flagged. {{S04}} {{S11}} {{S07}} {{S26}}

table.caption: Rent-increase review checklist — every control sourced

rows.item: Is the unit actually covered by the Rent Ordinance?
rows.value: Verify via the Property Information Map / Rent Board
rows.basis: "Many residential units built on or before June 13, 1979 have both rent control and eviction protection."

rows.item: Is a current Rent Increase License on file?
rows.value: Must be on file before the effective date
rows.basis: "A landlord must have a current rent increase license … before any annual or banked rent increase can go into effect."

rows.item: Is the increase on/after the 12-month anniversary?
rows.value: Yes — one increase per 12 months
rows.basis: "A landlord can impose the first annual increase 12 months after the date the tenant's lease began."

rows.item: Is the percentage the one in effect on the effective date?
rows.basis: "The landlord should use the percentage that will be in effect on the date of the increase …"

rows.item: Was the calculation on base rent only?
rows.value: Yes — no passthroughs, no rounding up
rows.basis: "Landlords must calculate the rent increase on the tenant's base rent only." "Rent increases cannot be rounded up to the nearest dollar."

rows.item: Was any banked increase properly computed?
rows.value: No compounding, no prorating, no rounding up; 24-month rule
rows.basis: "They cannot be compounded or prorated." "A skipped increase is only banked if at least 24 full months pass without any rent increase."

rows.item: Was a petition required and filed first?
rows.value: Only for the six petition categories
rows.basis: "For certain types of rent increases, landlords must file a petition at the Rent Board before serving the tenants with a notice of the increase."

rows.item: Did the written notice contain all required items?
rows.value: Dollar amount, percentage, effective date, allocation
rows.basis: SF Admin Code § 37.3(b) and Rent Board guidance.

rows.item: Was the correct notice period used and was it served properly?
rows.value: 30 days (90 if >10%); +5 days if mailed; personal delivery or § 1013 mail
rows.basis: Civil Code § 827.

rows.item: Was any part of the increase linked to an occupant change?
rows.value: Must be no
rows.basis: SF Admin Code § 37.3(a)(11)(A); "Any agreement to pay more rent is void and unenforceable by the landlord."

rows.item: Was the same neutral rule applied to both units?
rows.value: Documented in writing before service
rows.basis: Fair housing law prohibits different terms based on a protected characteristic.

rows.item: Was there any retaliatory purpose?
rows.value: Must be no
rows.basis: Government Code § 12955(f).

rows.item: Was a market-rate reset (§ 6.14 / Costa-Hawkins) used?
rows.value: Not available where an original occupant remains; co-tenants excluded
rows.basis: "This subdivision does not apply to partial changes in occupancy … where one or more of the occupants … remains an occupant in lawful possession."

rows.item: Actual licence / notice / rent-history documents for these two units
rows.basis: Not supplied. Left blank by rule; see Flagged for Review.

rows.item: Written opinion from a licensed tenant attorney
rows.basis: Not obtainable from an official source. Left blank by rule.

sections.heading: 3. What this project can and cannot conclude
sections.body: Can conclude: the applicable published rate, the notice and licence requirements, the timing rules, the petition categories, and the fair-housing constraints — all verified against official sources. Cannot conclude: that either unit is covered, that a licence exists, that a particular increase is lawful, or that a tenant lawyer would approve it. Those are listed on the Flagged for Review page with their official source links. {{S01}} {{S11}} {{S19}} {{F-03}} {{F-08}} {{F-11}}

rows.item: Published allowable rate
rows.basis: Rent Board announcement.

rows.item: Notice and licence requirements
rows.value: Verified
rows.basis: Civil Code § 827; SF Admin Code § 37.3(b); Housing Inventory rules.

rows.item: Lawfulness of a specific proposed increase
rows.basis: Requires the full file and a legal determination. Left blank by rule.

rows.item: Coverage confirmation for these units
rows.basis: Requires an official property-record lookup. Left blank by rule.
